climate_pressure: Below-average rainfall and drought during the period reviewed in 2022.
documented_impact: Pastoral households move seasonally in search of grazing and water, including between Namibia and Angola.
fcv_mediator: Concentration of users and increased pressure on scarce grazing and water resources.
possible_consequence: IFRC associates this movement with resource competition and conflict, without specifying conflict type, incidents or scale.
institutions: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
alternative_explanations: Land access, service provision, pre-existing resource arrangements and livelihood conditions also shape competition; mobility is an established risk-management practice.
uncertainty: Localized qualitative assessment. Conflict is unspecified and must not be read as armed violence, ethnic hostility or a general risk posed by migrants. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Pastoral mobility can manage climatic risk; water-system rehabilitation and cash assistance were reported separately, without evaluated conflict-prevention outcomes.
compact_statement: The 2022 IFRC assessment associates drought-related pastoral movement with resource competition and unspecified conflict, not an armed-conflict forecast.
